b: The Ashford Comets defeated the Amberley Stags 4-1 on Saturday, led by Jaffe's 3 goals. The result leaves Ashford first in the standings.

h: Unemployment in Oakhurst falls to 5.6 percent
b: The jobless rate in the Oakhurst area fell as hospitals added positions. The labor force participation rate was little changed.

h: Aldersgate Valley residents fight proposed quarry
b: Neighbors in Aldersgate Valley filled a township hearing to oppose a gravel quarry. The owner said it would employ forty people and restore the land after thirty years.

h: Rents in Kingsport rise 4 percent in a year
b: Average rent in Kingsport reached $1454 a month, according to a new survey. Tenant groups asked the council to consider a cap, while landlords pointed to higher taxes and insurance.

h: Bus drivers in Valemont protest schedule changes
b: Drivers for the Valemont transit authority wore armbands to work to protest split shifts. The union said it has not called a strike. Service ran normally, though 7 routes were cut at rush hour for lack of staff.

h: Senate approves Rural Broadband Act
b: The Rural Broadband Act cleared the Senate by 64 votes to 34 on Wednesday. Sponsor Senator Pellegrino said the vote shows broad support. The measure now goes to a conference committee, where differences over an offset for the cost must be settled.

h: New study links cooking at home to longer life
b: Researchers following 16,000 adults for 18 years found a lower risk of heart disease among those who walked 8,000 steps daily. The authors cautioned that the study shows association, not cause.

h: County treasurer's office moves to new building
b: The county treasurer's office will open in a renovated bank building next month. Residents can pay property taxes by card at the counter for the first time.

h: First snow of the season dusts Glenrock
b: 8 inches of wet snow fell on Glenrock and the surrounding hills overnight, the earliest measurable snowfall in 12 years. Plows were out by dawn and several flights were delayed.

h: Eriksen signs 3-year deal with Kestrels
b: The Kestrels locked up their star guard, Alvarado, with a contract reportedly worth $130 million. The player said he wanted to stay in Ashford.

h: Ironbridge clinic receives $3 million for rural care
b: A federal grant will pay for a mobile clinic, two nurse practitioners and telehealth carts serving farms around Ironbridge. Officials said the nearest emergency room is now 48 miles away for some families.

h: Senate rejects Border Technology Act on a procedural vote
b: The Border Technology Act failed to advance, getting 63 votes where sixty were required. Senator Kowalski, the majority leader, blamed delay tactics. A revised version could return after Thanksgiving.

h: Amberley Stags top Thornbury Foxes 2-1
b: The Amberley Stags defeated the Thornbury Foxes 2-1 on Sunday, led by Pellegrino's 2 goals. The result leaves Amberley first in the standings.

h: Merrow Pier footbridge reopens after cable repairs
b: The Merrow Pier footbridge reopened on Friday afternoon, nine days after inspectors found corroded suspension cables on its east side. Harbor officials said the replacement cables were rated for twice the load and that the lights along the deck had also been rewired.

h: Lane closures planned on Mill Road in Amberley
b: Expect one lane of traffic in each direction on Mill Road through Amberley from Monday until the end of the month, while a contractor lays new water mains. Businesses said they will stay open with signs for parking in back.

h: First snow of the season dusts Kingsport
b: 4 inches of wet snow fell on Kingsport and the surrounding hills overnight, the earliest measurable snowfall in 18 years. Plows were out by dawn and several flights were delayed.

h: Unemployment in Elkton falls to 3.9 percent
b: The jobless rate in the Elkton area fell as schools added positions. The labor force participation rate was little changed.

h: Alvarado signs 3-year deal with Wolverines
b: The Wolverines locked up their star forward, Rasmussen, with a contract reportedly worth $162 million. The player said he wanted to stay in Valemont.

h: Police in Elkton warn of phone scam targeting seniors
b: Callers pretending to be bank investigators have taken $159,000 from 10 older residents of Elkton this month. Officers urged families to hang up and call the bank directly.

h: Ironbridge clinic receives $4 million for rural care
b: A federal grant will pay for a mobile clinic, two nurse practitioners and telehealth carts serving farms around Ironbridge. Officials said the nearest emergency room is now 43 miles away for some families.

h: Amberley council weighs budget for bus shelters
b: The Amberley city council opened hearings on a $3.6 million proposal for school lunches. Residents spoke for two hours; a vote is expected on December 3.

h: Flood warning issued for Elkton
b: The weather service issued a flood warning for the river at Elkton, expected to crest 4 feet above flood stage on Thursday. Residents of low-lying streets were told to move vehicles and valuables.

h: Police in Corbin warn of phone scam targeting seniors
b: Callers pretending to be bank investigators have taken $70,000 from 21 older residents of Corbin this month. Officers urged families to hang up and call the bank directly.
